metadata.methods_description: Participants completed a resting-state recording of about 8 minutes (eyes open and closed periods of 63 s each), followed by four tasks in randomized order (words, faces, emotions, houses). Each task had a practice block and separate right-hand and left-hand response blocks (80 stimuli each, 160 total). Stimuli were shown for 1 s, followed by a fixation cross of 500-700 ms. Participants pressed the space bar only for target stimuli (animal names, female faces, houses with pitched roofs).

citation_details.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
citation_details.author: Junyu Pan, Ruicheng Yin, Bao‐Liang Lu, Dongsheng Li, Wei-Long Zheng, Yansen Wang
citation_details.abstract: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. Quark-G leads linear probing (LP) at 54.33%, a 1.24-point margin. Both also lead average task rank. At the last evaluated checkpoints, larger encoders improve Full-FT more consistently than LP, and stronger LP does not guarantee stronger Full-FT. citation_details.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
citation_details.author: Ryota Kanai
citation_details.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. citation_details.title: Hemispheric segregation is evident in early perception, not just higher cognition
citation_details.author: Petunia Reinke, Sebastian Ocklenburg
citation_details.abstract: Introduction: Functional hemispheric segregation, the organization of distinct cognitive functions into separate hemispheres, has so far been investigated mainly using behavioral measures or fMRI. Whether such segregation manifests at early perceptual stages, however, remains unknown. The present study is the first to test Gerrits' segregation bias model using EEG, examining lateralization of early ERP components (N1/N170) across language, face, and emotional face processing. Methods: The present study is based on an openly available EEG dataset obtained from OpenNeuro. We analyzed data from left-, mixed-, and right-handed participants to investigate the influence of handedness and sex on early functional hemispheric segregation. Hemispheric lateralization was assessed using early event-related potential components (N1/N170) across language, face, and emotional face processing tasks.
